First, risk aversion caused by hardness of learning: when the correct progress-making action is hard to learn but an easy cyclic action is available, the model puts relatively more probability on the cyclic action and gets stuck. Second, even when there is no hardness, Transformers show an inductive bias toward temporally correlated errors, so the same few actions keep being chosen and loops appear. Higher temperature reduces looping by promoting exploration, but it does not fix the errors in learning, so generations remain much longer than necessary at high temperature; in this sense, temperature is a stopgap rather than a holistic solution. We end with a discussion of training-time interventions aimed at directly reducing errors in learning.
items.author: Charilaos Pipis, Shivam Garg, Vasilis Kontonis, Vaishnavi Shrivastava, Akshay Krishnamurthy, Dimitris Papailiopoulos

items.title: Quantum-Classical Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Reservoir Seepage Equations
items.summary:
arXiv:2512.03923v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Solving reservoir seepage partial differential equations (PDEs) is critical for hydrocarbon development optimization and production forecasting. Conventional numerical solvers suffer from mesh errors and high computational cost. Standard Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are limited by inefficient parameters. They also face weak high-dimensional representation and poor nonlinear fitting ability. We adapt the Discrete Variable (DV)-Circuit Quantum-Classical Physics-Informed Neural Network (QCPINN) to tackle these drawbacks. This work applies the method to four representative reservoir seepage models. The models cover heterogeneous single-phase pressure diffusion. They also include nonlinear Buckley-Leverett two-phase waterflooding. Another case is adsorption-coupled convection-diffusion compositional flow. The last one refers to fully coupled pressure-saturation two-phase flow with exponential permeability heterogeneity. The QCPINN combines classical preprocessing and postprocessing networks with a DV quantum core. It leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to boost high-dimensional feature mapping. Physical constraints are embedded within the framework to guarantee physically consistent solutions. We evaluate three quantum circuit topologies including Cascade, Cross-mesh and Alternate. Numerical tests prove QCPINNs outperform classical PINNs in prediction accuracy, and the circuit topologies show case-specific performance with clear applicable ranges. This work verifies QCPINN's practicability for reservoir engineering. It bridges quantum computing research with oilfield industrial applications.
items.author: Xiang Rao, Yina Liu, Yuxuan Shen

items.title: Understanding Negative Learning in Large Language Model Fine-tuning
items.summary:
arXiv:2512.00778v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Negative learning has never been more important than it is today, particularly in large language model (LLM) fine-tuning, where it underpins machine unlearning, preference- and reward-based optimization, and exploratory data generation. Yet its functional role remains a subject of ongoing debate, with existing work variously characterizing it as forgetting, regularization, or target shaping. However, analytical support focuses primarily on the single-update scale, while empirical results at the trajectory scale are typically obtained under negative-only training and may not extend to composite objectives in which it interacts with other components. To develop a deeper understanding, we introduce a gradient-based endpoint probing framework that can examine negative updates separately throughout training. Our analysis reveals that negative learning plays different roles across algorithms and training phases. For example, in off-policy DPO, it acts more like a regularizer early in training and shows evidence of target shaping only toward out-of-distribution endpoints and only in later phases. In on-policy PPO and GRPO, by contrast, negative updates offset endpoint-aligned positive learning without stable target shaping, consistent with a role in sustaining exploration. Guided by these findings, we develop a family of stage-aware methods that modulate the strength of negative updates throughout training, improving fine-tuning performance across tasks.
items.author: Yue Wang, Qizhou Wang, Zizhuo Zhang, Gang Niu, Bo Han, Masashi Sugiyama

items.title: UMM-RM: An Upcycle-and-Merge MoE Reward Model for Mitigating Reward Hacking
items.summary:
arXiv:2512.00724v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Reward models (RMs) are critical to reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). However, policy models can exploit biases or spurious correlations in dense RMs, causing reward hacking: RM scores rise while alignment with human preferences deteriorates, especially under distribution shift. We propose UMM-RM (Upcycle-and-Merge MoE Reward Model), which copies the feed-forward layers of an SFT checkpoint to initialize shared and routed experts, then trains the model on preference data. The always-active shared expert captures instruction-agnostic preference signals, while routed experts model fine-grained preferences across instructions or tasks. The experts are then merged into a single dense RM using learnable weights, preserving the robustness and exploitation resistance of expert diversity without MoE or ensemble inference overhead. Across multiple base models and preference datasets, UMM-RM improves preference accuracy, reduces reward hacking during PPO training, and achieves more stable preference alignment than standard dense RMs.
items.author: Lingling Fu, Yongfu Xue

items.title: PISA: Prioritized Invariant Subgraph Aggregation for Out-of-Distribution Generalization on Graphs
items.summary:
arXiv:2511.22435v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Invariant learning on graphs aims to build predictors that rely on causal substructures rather than on environment-specific shortcuts. Current methods extract either a single invariant subgraph (CIGA) or, more recently, a set of diverse invariant subgraphs (SuGAr). We observe that the second half of the multi-subgraph pipeline, "how the extracted subgraphs are combined" has gone essentially unexamined; existing methods average branch predictions uniformly or select one greedily. We show that this is precisely where accuracy is lost. A minimum-variance combination argument establishes that uniform averaging is optimal only when every branch carries the same total error covariance with the ensemble---a knife edge balance that second order exchangeability guarantees and that the diversity regularizer used to obtain multiple subgraphs is explicitly designed to break. We then show that invariance is closed under post composition; because the branches are frozen and read the graph only through their invariant subgraphs, any measurable aggregator of their outputs remains invariant, and the aggregate's environment gap is bounded by the branches' residual invariance violation uniformly over aggregators. Learning the combination rule by plain empirical risk minimization is therefore safe, and aggregator capacity trades off against estimation error rather than robustness. PISA instantiates this with a lightweight instance-conditional MLP over stacked branch logits, trained on frozen branches at negligible cost. Across 15 synthetic and real benchmarks, PISA improves the average over the strongest prior method by 2.96 points on synthetic shifts and 1.74 points on realistic shifts, with per-dataset gains up to 5.90 points, and nearly doubles SuGAr's improvement over ERM on the six DrugOOD tasks (from +2.76 to +5.07 ROC-AUC).
items.author: Ali Ghasemi, Farooq Ahmad Wani, Maria Sofia Bucarelli, Fabrizio Silvestri

items.title: From Topology to Retrieval: Decoding Embedding Spaces with Unified Signatures
items.summary:
arXiv:2511.22150v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Studying the shape of text embedding spaces enhances our understanding of model behavior and how geometry affects downstream task performance. While a range of topological and geometric metrics have been explored, they are typically analyzed in isolation, and the connections between them remain largely unknown. In this paper, we present Unified Topological Signatures (UTS) for characterizing the structure of embedding spaces. We evaluate our method across a wide range of text embedding models and retrieval datasets, finding that it outperforms individual metrics in downstream performance prediction. Through several experiments, we demonstrate that the signatures characterize embedding spaces more accurately, improve the prediction of model-specific properties and biases, and reveal novel insights into representational similarity that challenge the global claims of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
items.author: Florian Rottach, William Rudman, Bastian Rieck, Harrisen Scells, Carsten Eickhoff

items.title: QuAnTS: Question Answering on Time Series
items.summary:
arXiv:2511.05124v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Text offers intuitive access to information. This can, in particular, complement the density of numerical time series, thereby enabling improved interactions with time series models to enhance accessibility and decision-making. While the creation of question-answering datasets and models has recently seen remarkable growth, most research focuses on question answering (QA) on vision and text, with time series receiving minute attention. To bridge this gap, we propose a challenging novel time series QA (TSQA) dataset, QuAnTS, for Question Answering on Time Series data. Specifically, we pose a wide variety of questions and answers about human motion in the form of tracked skeleton trajectories. We verify that the large-scale QuAnTS dataset is well-formed and comprehensive through extensive experiments. Thoroughly evaluating existing and newly proposed baselines then lays the groundwork for a deeper exploration of TSQA using QuAnTS. Additionally, we provide human performances as a key reference for gauging the practical usability of such models. We hope to encourage future research on interacting with time series models through text, enabling better decision-making and more transparent systems.
items.author: Felix Divo, Maurice Kraus, Anh Q. Nguyen, Hao Xue, Imran Razzak, Flora D. Salim, Kristian Kersting, Devendra Singh Dhami

items.title: A Nesterov-Accelerated Byzantine-Robust Federated Learning
items.summary:
arXiv:2511.02657v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We investigate robust federated learning, where a group of workers collaboratively train a shared model under the orchestration of a central server in the presence of Byzantine adversaries capable of arbitrary and potentially malicious behaviors. To simultaneously enhance communication efficiency and resilience against such adversaries, we propose a Byzantine-resilient Nesterov-accelerated federated learning (Byrd-NAFL) algorithm. Byrd-NAFL seamlessly integrates Nesterov's momentum into the federated learning process alongside Byzantine-resilient aggregation rules to achieve fast and safe convergence against gradient corruption. We establish a finite-time convergence guarantee for Byrd-NAFL under non-convex and smooth loss functions with relaxed assumptions on the aggregated gradients. Extensive numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of Byrd-NAFL and demonstrate the superiority over existing benchmarks in terms of convergence speed, accuracy, and resilience to diverse malicious attacks.
items.author: Lihan Xu, Xiaoyi Fan, Gang Wang, Runhao Zeng, Xiping Hu, Yanjie Dong

items.title: The Optimization Landscape of Carath\'eodory Decomposition of Toeplitz Covariances
items.summary:
arXiv:2511.01605v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Toeplitz covariance estimation is a classical signal processing problem, yet the geometry of the Gaussian maximum-likelihood objective remains only partially understood. Recent Newton-type, majorization-minimization, and gradient-based methods often solve the nonconvex problem globally with enough samples, but also reveal a difficult computational landscape. We study this phenomenon through an overparameterized Carath\'eodory representation, which parameterizes the covariance by the frequencies and amplitudes of steering vectors. A simple example shows that, for any uniform frequency grid, optimizing only the amplitudes can leave a positive error even in the population setting, which motivates optimizing the frequencies as well. Our main result proves that this nonlinear parameterization adds no stationary points: for any sample covariance, every stationary point with a positive definite covariance gives a stationary point of the Toeplitz maximum-likelihood problem. In the population setting, every such point therefore recovers the true covariance. We also prove that gradient descent converges to the true covariance in the population setting, and to the unique maximum likelihood estimate when the sample covariance is close enough to the true covariance. These results do not require overparameterization. Numerically, overparameterization speeds up gradient descent and gives a more accurate estimate for a fixed number of iterations.
items.author: Daniel Busbib, Ami Wiesel

items.title: Reviving Stale Updates: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Asynchronous Federated Learning
items.summary:
arXiv:2511.00655v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without sharing raw data, yet its scalability is limited by synchronization overhead. Asynchronous federated learning (AFL) alleviates this issue by allowing clients to communicate independently, thereby improving wall-clock efficiency in large-scale, hardware-heterogeneous environments. However, asynchrony introduces updates computed on outdated global models (staleness) that can destabilize optimization and hinder convergence. We propose FedRevive, an AFL framework that revives stale updates through data-free knowledge distillation (DFKD). FedRevive integrates parameter-space aggregation with a server-side DFKD process that transfers knowledge from stale client updates to the current global model without access to data. A meta-learned generator synthesizes pseudo-samples for multi-teacher distillation. A hybrid aggregation scheme combining raw with DFKD updates effectively mitigates staleness while retaining AFL scalability. Experiments on vision and text benchmarks show that FedRevive achieves faster training by up to 29.7% and higher final accuracy by up to 11.4 percentage points than baselines.
items.author: Baris Askin, Holger R. Roth, Zhenyu Sun, Carlee Joe-Wong, Gauri Joshi, Ziyue Xu

items.title: Deep Jump Gaussian Processes for Surrogate Modeling of High-Dimensional Piecewise Continuous Functions
items.summary:
arXiv:2510.21974v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We introduce Deep Jump Gaussian Processes (DJGP), a novel method for surrogate modeling of a piecewise continuous function on a high-dimensional domain. DJGP addresses the limitations of conventional Jump Gaussian Processes (JGP) in high-dimensional input spaces by integrating region-specific, locally linear projections with JGP modeling. These projections employ region-dependent matrices to capture local low-dimensional subspace structures, making them well suited to the inherently localized modeling behavior of JGPs, a variant of local Gaussian processes. To control model complexity, we place a Gaussian Process prior on the projection matrices, allowing them to evolve smoothly across the input space. The projected inputs are then modeled with a JGP to capture piecewise continuous relationships with the response. This yields a distinctive two-layer deep learning of GP/JGP. We further develop a scalable variational inference algorithm to jointly learn the projection matrices and JGP hyperparameters. Rigorous theoretical analysis and extensive empirical studies are provided to justify the proposed approach. In particular, we derive an oracle error bound for DJGP and decompose it into four distinct sources of error, which are then linked to practical implications. Experiments on synthetic and benchmark datasets demonstrate that DJGP achieves superior predictive accuracy and more reliable uncertainty quantification compared with existing methods.
items.author: Yang Xu, Chiwoo Park

items.title: Stochastic Difference-of-Convex Optimization with Momentum
items.summary:
arXiv:2510.17503v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We study the online stochastic difference-of-convex (DC) program $\min_{x \in R^n} F(x) = G(x) - H(x) + r_1(x) - r_2(x)$, which covers sparse learning with nonconvex penalties, robust regression with smooth robust losses, and non-negative positive--unlabeled learning. We propose \emph{momentum-based DCA} (MDCA), which combines a damped DCA step with a momentum estimator for $\nabla H$ and uses a constant per-iteration batch size. With exact solutions of the convex subproblems, MDCA with Polyak momentum uses $\mathcal{O}( \epsilon^{-4})$ stochastic gradients of $H$ to reach $\epsilon$-stationarity, and momentum-based variance reduction (MVR) uses $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-3})$ under averaged smoothness, with a single $\mathcal O(\epsilon^{-1})$ warm-up batch in place of the periodic large batches of DCA-PAGE, whose $\epsilon$-dependence it matches. We also introduce a single-loop variant (S-MDCA) that replaces the subproblem solve by one stochastic prox-gradient step; for every fixed smoothing parameter $\gamma$ for which the separately smoothed surrogate $F_\gamma$ is bounded below, it reaches $\epsilon$-stationarity of $F_\gamma$ in $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-4})$ iterations, which does not by itself imply stationarity of $F$. A variance--drift trade-off lemma describes how the momentum parameter trades estimator variance against iterate-drift bias in steady-state upper bounds. Guarantees are given for two criteria: the critical-distance measure, and a DCA fixed-point residual that requires no smoothness of $r_2$ and vanishes exactly at DC-critical points; both give the same $\epsilon$-dependence. Experiments on two LIBSVM classification datasets illustrate the methods' behaviour.
items.author: El Mahdi Chayti, Martin Jaggi

items.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation through Latent Subspace Coefficients Search
items.summary:
arXiv:2510.11068v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Real-world deployment often exposes vision models to distribution shifts, making test-time adaptation (TTA) important for reliable prediction. Existing TTA methods can be difficult to deploy on edge devices because they require backpropagation, activation storage, or test-time batches, which increase computation, memory, and state. We propose \textbf{ELaTTA} (\textit{Efficient Latent Test-Time Adaptation}), a forward-only, gradient-free framework for single-instance TTA. ELaTTA freezes the pretrained model and adapts each test input by searching a low-dimensional coefficient vector in a principal latent subspace computed offline from a source-domain cache. The basis is stored once and source data are discarded before deployment. At test time, CMA-ES performs covariance-adaptive Gaussian search, ranks candidate corrections by prediction entropy, and selects the best candidate within a fixed evaluation budget. On five visual benchmarks spanning corruption, natural, rendition, sketch, and cross-domain shifts, ELaTTA provides strong accuracy under strict and continual single-instance protocols. In the strict single-instance comparison, MEMO requires \emph{64.7$\times$} the computation and \emph{12.4$\times$} the peak memory of ELaTTA. A complementary keyword-spotting experiment shows that the same coefficient-search design transfers beyond vision. We further demonstrate ViT-Base adaptation on a Raspberry Pi 5, confirming the feasibility of deploying ELaTTA on an edge device.
items.author: Xinyu Luo, Jie Liu, Kecheng Chen, Yihua Shao, Junyi Yang, Bo Ding, Nicu Sebe, Arindam Basu, Haoliang Li

items.title: Bayesian Optimization under Uncertainty for Training a Scale Parameter in Stochastic Models
items.summary:
arXiv:2510.06439v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Hyperparameter tuning is a challenging problem especially when the system itself involves uncertainty. Due to noisy function evaluations, optimization under uncertainty can be computationally expensive. In this paper, we present a novel Bayesian optimization framework tailored for hyperparameter tuning under uncertainty, with a focus on optimizing a scale- or precision-type parameter in stochastic models. The proposed method employs a statistical surrogate for the underlying random variable, enabling analytical evaluation of the expectation operator. Moreover, we derive a closed-form expression for the optimizer of the random acquisition function, which significantly reduces computational cost per iteration. Numerical experiments demonstrate substantial gains in optimization efficiency: about 40-fold reduction in data usage relative to a Monte Carlo-based one-dimensional optimization scheme, and an order of magnitude improvement relative to a Gaussian process-based Bayesian optimization baseline.
items.author: Akash Yadav, Ruda Zhang

items.title: JaGNet: Detection, Identification and Position Error Correction of GNSS Jamming with Deep Temporal Graphs
items.summary:
arXiv:2509.14000v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) underpin location-dependent mobile computing, such as railway signaling, public transport and fleet tracking, yet face growing disruption from low-cost jammers. Under moderate jamming, low-cost receivers keep reporting a valid fix, shifted by up to several meters and often without an interference flag. Their built-in defenses run in closed firmware, and existing data-driven position error correction methods are designed for multipath, require raw pseudoranges or operate on single epochs. We propose JaGNet, a single-layer heterogeneous graph convolutional LSTM over star graphs of the receiver and its satellites, which, from the standard receiver output alone, detects the jamming, identifies its type and power, and corrects the reported position only when jamming is detected. We evaluate it on new hardware-in-the-loop recordings of a commercial multi-constellation receiver under three jammer types at six powers, at six static locations and on eleven railway and bus routes. JaGNet detects 99.8 to 99.9% of the jammed 10-s windows with at most 1.0% false positives, against 64.7 to 66.2% for the receiver's own monitor, and identifies the jammer type in 95.2 to 96.6% of them. Trained in the laboratory only, it detects 97.7% of the Jammertest 2024 field windows with a C/N0 drop of 10 dB or more. It reduces the mean absolute position error by 67.5% at held-out locations and by 64.0% on held-out route repetitions, where its error is 20.2 cm below that of the strongest baseline, whereas at the static locations the attention-based baselines are within 0.4 cm of it.
items.author: Ivana Kesi\'c, Alja\v{z} Blatnik, Carolina Fortuna, Bla\v{z} Bertalani\v{c}

items.title: Bouncy particle sampler with infinite exchanging parallel tempering
items.summary:
arXiv:2509.02003v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Markov chain Monte Carlo is one of the most useful tools for obtaining samples from complex distributions, such as posterior distributions in Bayesian inference. Bouncy particle sampler (BPS) is a method that performs sampling using uniform linear motion and elastic collisions. Since BPS does not require time discretization, it is expected to be more advantageous than the widely used Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) and Langevin Monte Carlo (LMC) for distributions with large curvature changes. To sample more efficiently from multimodal distributions, we propose BPS with parallel tempering (BPS-PT) in the infinite exchange limit, based on LMC-PT with the infinite exchange rate proposed in a previous study. Using a distribution with large curvature changes, BPS-PT showed estimation accuracy comparable to HMC-PT and LMC-PT, and achieved higher ESS per computational time. Therefore, BPS-PT is considered to be effective for distributions with large curvature changes.
items.author: Yohei Saito, Shun Kimura, Koujin Takeda

items.title: A Note on Graphon-Signal Analysis of Graph Neural Networks
items.summary:
arXiv:2508.18564v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: A recent paper, ``A Graphon-Signal Analysis of Graph Neural Networks'', by Levie, analyzed message passing graph neural networks (MPNNs) by embedding the input space of MPNNs, i.e., attributed graphs (graph-signals), into a space of attributed graphons (graphon-signals). Based on extensions of standard results in graphon analysis to graphon-signals, the paper proved a generalization bound and a sampling lemma for MPNNs. However, there are some missing ingredients in that paper, limiting its applicability in practical settings of graph machine learning. In the current paper, we introduce several refinements and extensions to existing results that address these shortcomings. In detail, 1) we extend the main results in the paper to graphon-signals with multidimensional signals (rather than 1D signals), 2) we extend the Lipschitz continuity to MPNNs with readout with respect to cut distance (rather than MPNNs without readout with respect to cut metric), 3) we improve the generalization bound by utilizing robustness-type generalization bounds, and 4) we extend the analysis to non-symmetric graphons and kernels.
items.author: Levi Rauchwerger, Ron Levie

items.title: Cross-Subject and Cross-Montage EEG Transfer Learning via Individual Tangent Space Alignment and Spatial-Riemannian Feature Fusion
items.summary:
arXiv:2508.08216v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Personalised music-based interventions offer a powerful means of supporting motor rehabilitation by dynamically tailoring auditory stimuli to provide external timekeeping cues, modulate affective states, and stabilise gait patterns. Generalisable Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) thus hold promise for adapting these interventions across individuals. However, inter-subject variability in EEG signals, further compounded by movement-induced artefacts and motor planning differences, hinders the generalisability of BCIs and results in lengthy calibration processes. We propose Individual Tangent Space Alignment (ITSA), a novel pre-alignment strategy incorporating subject-specific recentering, distribution matching, and supervised rotational alignment to enhance cross-subject generalisation. Our hybrid architecture fuses Regularised Common Spatial Patterns (RCSP) with Riemannian geometry in parallel and sequential configurations, improving class separability while maintaining the geometric structure of covariance matrices for robust statistical computation. Using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, `ITSA' demonstrates significant performance improvements across subjects and conditions. The parallel fusion approach shows the greatest enhancement over its sequential counterpart, with robust performance maintained across varying data conditions and electrode configurations. The code will be made publicly available at the time of publication.
items.author: Nicole Lai-Tan, Xiao Gu, Marios G. Philiastides, Fani Deligianni

items.title: Signature-Kernel One-Class Learning with Manifold Regularisation for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
items.summary:
arXiv:2507.23449v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: One-class learning is an effective methodology for time series anomaly detection, yet kernel one-class approaches often compare sequences in a pointwise fashion and ignore the geometry of normal data. In this work, we present a manifold-regularised, large-margin $\ell_p$-support vector data description ($\ell_p$-SVDD) method that analyses sequences as paths via the signature kernel. By incorporating a a graph-Laplacian penalty into the $\ell_p$-SVDD objective function and utilising the representer theorem for manifold regularisation, we illustrate that the dual task retains the functional form of the original one with a modified kernel matrix. As such, existing Frank--Wolfe solvers can be applied unchanged. We show that this new modified kernel is a valid kernel matrix and under a generic norm bound on the discriminant, the proposed model yields a smaller Rademacher-complexity bound than the baseline. Furthermore, the signature kernel which is computed through a Goursat partial differential equation and can handle irregularly sampled data and is invariant to reparametrisation has not previously been used for one-class time series anomaly detection to the best of our knowledge. Our experiments on five widely used benchmarks, evaluated without point adjustment, demonstrate that the proposed approach compares very favourably with the state of the art approaches.
items.author: Shervin Rahimzadeh Arashloo

items.title: PVD-ONet: A Multi-scale Neural Operator Method for Singularly Perturbed Boundary Layer Problems
items.summary:
arXiv:2507.21437v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks and physics-informed DeepONet excel at solving partial differential equations but often struggle with singularly perturbed problems. To address this limitation, we propose two novel data-free frameworks: the Prandtl--Van Dyke neural network(PVD-Net) and its operator-learning extension, the Prandtl--Van Dyke Deep Operator Network(PVD-ONet). Each framework provides leading-order and high-order versions to meet different modeling requirements. The leading-order PVD-Net integrates Prandtl's matching condition for improved stability, while the high-order PVD-Net employs Van Dyke's matching principle to capture fine-scale boundary layer structures with higher accuracy. Extending PVD-Net to operator learning, PVD-ONet enables efficient prediction for families of boundary layer problems without retraining. Numerical experiments on representative one- and two-dimensional problems demonstrate that the proposed methods outperform existing baselines. Beyond forward prediction, the framework also supports inverse problems by inferring the scaling exponent governing boundary layer thickness from sparse observations, highlighting its potential for practical applications.
items.author: Tiantian Sun, Jian Zu

items.title: Inexact calculus of variations on the hyperspherical tangent bundle with connections to the attention mechanism
items.summary:
arXiv:2507.15431v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We offer a theoretical mathematical background through Lagrangian optimization on the unit hyperspherical manifold and its tangential structure. Our methods can be categorized as inexact since our methods are projection-based and since we will perturb the functional optimization with epsilon-type quantities. We draw connections to the attention mechanism and the Transformer since it exists as a flow map in the tangent fiber for each token along the high-dimensional unit sphere. Our motivation for this work is primarily twofold: we study the attention mechanism under its flow map and its relations to traditional calculus of variations and Lagrangian optimization; and we study several calculus problems of variations on the unit hypersphere that appeal to a broader mathematical lens in approximating, variational contexts.
items.author: Andrew Gracyk

items.title: Understanding the Interplay between Memorization and Learning in Large Language Models
items.summary:
arXiv:2507.14777v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We investigate foundational questions about the interplay between memorization and learning in large language models (LLMs). When an LLM generates a string, can we disentangle the roles of rote memorization and contextual learning? Rote memorization results in an LLM regurgitating specific details of a training string, while contextual learning leads to the generation of new strings that follow generalizable patterns of the underlying language. Related questions of interest include: can an LLM avoid memorization when optimally learning a language?, and if not, can we design training schemes to reduce memorization and improve learning?
  To address these questions, we propose contextual memorization, a new measure that precisely disentangles memorization from learning. Using this measure, we establish that different training strings are memorized at different epochs in training, and that memorization of some training strings is unavoidable when optimally learning a language. Finally, we propose memorization-aware training, a scheme that dynamically down-samples training strings based on their memorization, and in doing so, equalizes learning across strings, reduces memorization, and improves learning. Our conclusions are supported by extensive experiments on multiple LLMs using formal languages as a controlled testbed, enabling precise language specification, exact string sampling, and elimination of data contamination; and further validated on natural languages.
items.author: Bishwamittra Ghosh, Soumi Das, Qinyuan Wu, Mohammad Aflah Khan, Deepak Garg, Krishna P. Gummadi, Evimaria Terzi

items.title: v2.1.299
items.summary:
What's changed

  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FILE_MENTIONS environment variable: Claude gets the paths of @ file mentions to read with its file tools, not the files' contents
  • Added idle compaction in the terminal: a 200K+ token conversation left idle for about 54 minutes is compacted before its one-hour prompt cache expires, so your next message doesn't reprocess it all
  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS to change idle compaction's 200K-token minimum; "idleCompaction": false in settings.json turns it off. Both need v2.1.290 or later
  • Added $.prompt.media so a prompt.submit hook of a mod installed by managed settings can read the bytes of an image or document attached to the prompt
  • Added $.session.identity() for mods installed by managed settings: how the session is signed in, and its organization and email when managed forceLoginOrgUUID lists that organization
  • Added size, weight, mono and tabular to a mod's Text and named spacing steps (xs to xl) to its Box; bold is deprecated in favor of weight
  • Added --shutdown-drain-sec to claude self-hosted-runner orchestrator: on SIGTERM it stops polling and gives the poll in flight and running spawn hooks up to that many seconds to finish
  • Added the skill's frontmatter, source, plugin name and file path to what a mod's skill.prompt hook receives
  • Added /effort and /fast in agent view to set what new sessions start with; a bare /model, /effort or /fast there now opens a picker
  • Added a "safe mode" line to the agents view peek panel for background sessions started with --safe-mode
  • Added a one-time note when plan mode won't ask before most edits or commands because bypass permissions is available
  • Added --disallow-tools and a disallowed_tools case field to claude plugin eval to keep specific built-in tools, such as Agent, out of eval runs
  • Added support for turning off the attribution block in Claude Desktop's Code tab: set CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0 in the env of a Claude apps gateway's code policy
  • Added a field to the attribution block in Claude Code sessions behind a Claude apps gateway; remove the block with CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0
  • Added a queue door to the session.append mod hook, so a mod can make the transcript's queue records differ from the prompt as sent
  • Added a note in /plugin and claude plugin validate naming a mod's hooks that are skipped where an organization manages Claude Code
  • Added /usage warnings for max effort, workflows, always-on context and large tool results
  • Fixed the error for a denied cloud session, which could point to the wrong organization when a key from apiKeyHelper was in use
  • Fixed sessions on a gateway-specific model name behind a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL ending with "Prompt is too long · automatic compaction failed" near 200K tokens instead of sending the request
  • Fixed a mod that submits a prompt at the end of every turn keeping a headless run going past --max-turns, --max-budget-usd, an interrupt, or the end of the host's conversation
  • Fixed cloud sessions sometimes showing the model's follow-up text after a tool group's one-line label
  • Fixed the Write and Edit tools creating a mod in a session's mods folder without asking in accept-edits mode when the config directory's path has no .claude in it
  • Fixed installed mods that kept running in an open session after being turned off remotely; they now unload between turns
  • Fixed Edit and Retry in Cowork and claude.ai cloud sessions failing on a message stopped while its UserPromptSubmit or mod prompt.submit hooks were still running (regression in 2.1.296)
  • Fixed an agent teammate started without a description keeping part of a credential from its prompt in the task description shown for it
  • Fixed the claude.ai view of a Remote Control or cloud session freezing when a large batch of events could not finish uploading over a slow connection
  • Fixed a sandboxed shell command being able to write into a --plugin-dir folder, whose code Claude Code reloads and runs outside the sandbox
  • Fixed memory growth under heavy debug logging (--debug, --debug-file), and a hang on exit when the debug log is on a disk or network mount that stops accepting writes
  • Fixed memory growing without bound when debug output goes to stderr and the parent process stops reading it
  • Fixed rm prompts on shell -c scripts that don't run rm. An rm built at run time in a script Claude Code can't read no longer prompts unless CLAUDE_CODE_STRICT_INLINE_SHELL_RM_PROMPT=1
  • Fixed double-clicking a word in an expanded transcript row in fullscreen mode collapsing the row instead of selecting the word
  • Fixed claude mcp list, claude doctor and /status reporting an empty .mcp.json as invalid
  • Fixed /btw jumping the transcript to the bottom when asked while scrolled up in fullscreen
  • Fixed sandboxed commands failing on WSL2 with bwrap: Can't mkdir /mnt/c/Program Files/ClaudeCode when the sandbox can write to the Windows drive
  • Fixed scheduled wakeups (ScheduleWakeup) not firing while a background task was running in Agent SDK, IDE and claude remote-control sessions
  • Fixed a mod's prompt.submit rewrite being silently dropped, sending the prompt as typed, for some prompts with a pasted image or an image that can't be read
  • Fixed a Remote Control prompt being lost when another queued prompt in the same batch failed to deliver
  • Fixed a Remote Control prompt that had passed its hooks being dropped from prompt history when Stop interrupted the next queued prompt's hook
  • Fixed sign-in, MCP servers and project trust appearing lost on Linux after a sandboxed command left an empty .config.json in the config directory
  • Fixed /sandbox reporting success when its setting could not be saved because the project folder is not writable; it now says nothing changed and why
  • Fixed SDK and headless sessions staying in auto mode after the host switched to a model that doesn't support auto mode
  • Fixed MCP servers named constructor or prototype in an MCP config never being connected
  • Fixed tools of an MCP server named constructor or toString asking for permission in auto mode and bypass permissions mode
  • Fixed a spurious "synced[0] commands path not found" plugin error at startup when another Claude Code process had just updated a claude.ai-synced plugin
  • Fixed the Artifact tool advising a retry when a publish that requests connectors or other access was refused by the server or a proxy (HTTP 403); it now says so and what to tell the user
  • Fixed Cowork cloud sessions staying on an old account plugin after a plugin reload that timed out or a restart that reused a recent sync
  • Fixed document blocks being dropped from your own message sent while Claude is working
  • Fixed Claude in Chrome asking for permission while no browser is connected; it now says the extension is not connected
  • Fixed the fullscreen "Update installed" notice being hidden behind the idle "/clear to save tokens" hint; it now shows beside the hint
  • Fixed a mod hook, with or without a .catch, being run again without end when it waits on another mod's noun that does its work outside the call
  • Fixed the Claude apps gateway serving models that a policy's availableModelsMatch: exact or deniedModels blocks; it now answers 400 and leaves them out of its model lists
  • Fixed the server-managed settings request to Anthropic carrying a third-party gateway's API key when a managed settings file sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
  • Fixed streams through a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL being aborted after 180 seconds with no data arriving; they now wait 300 seconds, whether or not feature flags are loaded
  • Fixed a mod's tool.describe or prompt.section answer that changed after $.ui.invalidate never reaching Claude; the new answer is now sent on the next turn
  • Fixed a settings file being ignored when enabledMcpjsonServers or disabledMcpjsonServers held a single server name (letters, digits, - or _) as a plain string
  • Fixed claude plugin test pausing a hook's time budget while a served $ method it had called kept making $ calls after answering
  • Fixed high memory use after resuming a cloud or Remote Control session that had run many subagents
  • Fixed plugin hooks being skipped when they pass a very deeply nested tool input or message on with next()
  • Fixed a value a mod's hook passes to next(), returns, or sends to a $ method being refused whole when one of its getters throws a RangeError; now only that key is refused
  • Fixed /usage, the approaching-limit warning (terminal and VS Code) and the status line sometimes showing more than 100% used (#92238)
  • Fixed wrapped text mixing CJK or emoji with Latin words losing its last line or leaving a blank row at some terminal widths
  • Fixed a cloud session sometimes ignoring the answer to a permission prompt or a question when the answer was given while the session's worker was being replaced
  • Fixed bold, italic and other nested text styles running over table borders or being lost on wrapped rows
  • Fixed Cowork cloud sessions running the old version of an account plugin changed, removed or disabled from another device until the session restarted
  • Fixed deny and ask rules for an MCP server (mcp__<server>) not applying when the server's normalized name contains a double underscore
  • Fixed long conversations losing newly attached images on every turn after one oversized image was refused by the API
  • Fixed the plugin_loaded telemetry event reporting has_hooks as false for plugins whose hooks are a hooks module, built-in plugins included
  • Fixed images attached while Claude is working (VS Code, desktop app, SDK) being sent at full size, which led to repeated image errors in long conversations
  • Fixed the image coordinate hint being missing or slightly off for large near-square images on newer models
  • Fixed feature flag, startup, fast mode, profile and feedback requests to Anthropic carrying the API key configured for a third-party gateway (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL); Anthropic API keys are still sent
  • Fixed a mod's hot reload ignoring a fix saved right after a failed reload; saving a mod file without changing it no longer reloads the mod
  • Fixed mods loaded from source files being refused when a hook hands $ to a function declaration imported from another file of the mod
  • Fixed a regression in 2.1.296 where cloud and headless sessions could run an approved tool call twice if a new message arrived as the session resumed after a restart
  • Fixed scheduled tasks being announced for the wrong minute: the scheduling tools now report each job's actual next run time
  • Fixed mods' hooks being handed values with __proto__ keys silently removed, which could skip a tool.check guard on a tool call another mod made
  • Fixed claude -p saying nothing when a settings file fails validation: text-output runs now list the file and the invalid entry on stderr
  • Fixed long pastes in terminals without bracketed paste losing all text after an invisible control character, such as a mis-decoded curly quote
  • Fixed managed settings and organization policy not being fetched when the stored login's plan was changed locally on machines whose MDM or managed-settings file sets forceLoginOrgUUID
  • Fixed MCP connections over HTTP hanging for 30 seconds and failing when a server never ends the body of its reply to a notification (#99014)
  • Fixed MCP servers added to a running headless or SDK session being connected before some policy checks ran; a blocked server is now reported as failed without being contacted
  • Fixed claude mcp list, claude mcp get and subagent MCP servers starting a server that a policy check blocks; it is now reported as blocked without being started
  • Fixed /reload-plugins not loading a plugin installed from another terminal a moment earlier
  • Fixed blank rows appearing under CJK and emoji text squeezed into a one-cell column, as in a very narrow terminal
  • Fixed text cut in the middle beside wide characters leaving a cell unused or being cut twice, and an emoji vanishing where a color changed inside it
  • Fixed bare mode notices in background sessions telling you to restart without --bare, which keeps the mode; they now name /stop and claude --resume, as safe mode ones do
  • Fixed ← not saying why it stayed put over a queued message while Remote Control is on
  • Fixed $.http.fetch in mods refusing a 304, 204 or 205 response that declares a Content-Length over the 4 MiB body limit
  • Fixed /config push notification toggles sending your account the previous setting instead of the one you just chose
  • Fixed a cloud session leaving a reply unfinished when its worker was replaced just after the reply hit the output token limit
  • Fixed Read failing on PDF page ranges in remote sessions on Linux that run without elevated privileges
  • Fixed Enter answering a question or permission prompt that had been held back while you typed an unsent message
  • Fixed a file attached to a message in a remote session being left out when its download stalled part way; the download is now tried again
  • Fixed queued prompts sent as content blocks over --input-format stream-json running together without a line break when merged into one turn
  • Fixed self-hosted runner sessions shutting down MCP servers added through an --exec-path wrapper's own --mcp-config when connectors change mid-session
  • Fixed claude plugin eval passing runs that the API refused: a run that ends on an API error now scores 0 without grading and makes the suite exit 1
  • Fixed permission prompts cutting off or wrapping too early when the reason text contains keycap or joined emoji
  • Fixed forceLoginOrgUUID and forceLoginMethod from MDM or the managed-settings file being hidden or replaced by server-managed settings
  • Fixed --bare sessions leaving out an MCP server named constructor or prototype that --channels asked for
  • Fixed resuming a conversation from before /clear reattaching to the Remote Control session of the conversation after it
  • Fixed a prompt starting with /, sent with the Agent SDK's verbatimPrompts option, running as a slash command when CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN re-ran it after a restart
  • Fixed background sessions started with --safe-mode silently leaving safe mode when the session was woken or restarted
  • Fixed scheduled tasks and loops firing again after every turn, or firing early, during the repeated hour when daylight saving time ends
  • Fixed the diff view listing a new file whose name begins or ends with a space under the wrong name
  • Fixed MCP tool calls in headless and SDK sessions sometimes failing or running twice when a background reconnect closed the connection they were running on
  • Fixed /btw side questions in non-interactive sessions not being cancelled when the session ends, and running a second time when the same request arrived again mid-run
  • Fixed sandboxed commands on macOS being able to read or write a denied path by its real location when the denied path passes through a symlink
  • Fixed sandbox denyRead and allowRead globs with braces, parentheses or backslashes in a folder's name being read differently by Claude Code's settings checks than by the sandbox
  • Fixed sandbox glob allowRead and allowWrite entries not being re-checked when the directory they start from is replaced by a symlink
  • Fixed worktree-isolated sessions accepting some awk programs the isolation guard should refuse
  • Fixed claude mcp add <name> -- <command> --background being started as a background session
  • Fixed a prompt or reply of --bg or --background to a background session being taken for the flag, which could start new sessions over and over instead of delivering it
  • Fixed a custom slash command's embedded shell line running twice when a newer message interrupted the command while its prompt was being checked
  • Fixed --worktree sessions leaving a folder behind in .git/worktrees in repositories using git's reftable ref storage
  • Fixed claude self-hosted-runner sessions using Anthropic-managed git showing tracked files as staged deletions when starting in a reused clone whose remote is still empty
  • Fixed Ultracode not being announced to scheduled tasks and other delivered headless turns when ultracode is on in settings
  • Fixed MCP OAuth sign-in, token refresh and sign-out not sending configured headers/headersHelper values, which broke servers behind an authenticating proxy
  • Fixed the Artifact tool reporting a spurious one-line difference against the live page, and refusing the publish, when a large page with a line break after <head> is published again unchanged
  • Fixed $.ui.open reporting a mod's pane as placed in sessions where no surface draws it, such as Claude Code for VS Code and claude -p
  • Fixed the agent.spawn mod hook not running when a finished subagent or a killed teammate is resumed: the hook's event now carries resume, and a mod can refuse it
  • Fixed claude plugin validate rejecting a mod's $.state references when plugin.json has no types key and the contract is at ./types/index.d.ts
  • Fixed a mod's dimColor text looking the same as plain text under the dark ANSI theme and on 16-color terminals
  • Fixed plan mode running a write (an MCP tool's, a file's, a shell command's) that a PreToolUse hook or a mod's tool.check hook allowed
  • Fixed background subagents in auto mode sometimes sending their final report twice, once as the result and once as a message
  • Fixed SendMessage not finding a subagent by name after the CLI restarted and resumed the session (names given before the last compaction still need the agent ID)
  • Fixed replies cut off at the output token limit ending the turn silently, with no retry or error, after a request fell back to non-streaming mode
  • Fixed Read garbling UTF-16LE files with a byte-order mark, and Write dropping byte-order marks or silently converting Windows-1252, Shift-JIS, GBK or UTF-16BE files to UTF-8 (now refused)
  • Fixed cloud sessions sometimes leaving a message unanswered when the worker was replaced right after a compaction
  • Fixed cloud sessions and CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN sometimes answering a finished turn again after a restart, when a tool ended the turn and a skill loaded in the same step
  • Fixed photos sent over Remote Control being dropped when their copy could not be saved on your computer; Claude now still sees the photo
  • Fixed files sent over Remote Control sometimes not arriving in long-running sessions
  • Fixed files of 30 to 35 MiB sent over Remote Control or to a cloud session not arriving
  • Fixed a user-installed mod's $.env.set changing the environment or shell prefix that command hooks from managed settings start with
  • Windows: Fixed the process-liveness check leaving orphaned PowerShell processes behind on busy machines until memory ran out
  • Windows: Fixed PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks that set no shell failing open when Git for Windows isn't installed; a guard that fails now blocks the call
  • Windows: Fixed Bash commands failing with "command not found" for a whole session when Git Bash did not report its PATH at startup
  • Self-hosted runner: Improved what setup and doctor say when the runner's machine has no git credentials
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed sessions that wrote output before their first turn being left with no release timer, ignoring --retire-at and delaying shutdown
  • Improved the error shown when a cloud session is refused because your claude.ai login was rejected or has expired: it now tells you to sign in again with claude auth login
  • Improved enforcement of managed permission rules, managed hooks and organization MCP tool names against user-installed mods
  • Improved memory and disk use when PDFs are @-mentioned: their bytes are no longer kept in the session transcript
  • Improved sandboxed Bash on Linux: Esc and Ctrl-C now work while wildcard read rules are being expanded for a command
  • Improved the startup warning for an unrecognized model ID: it is now one short line under the welcome banner with a docs link, instead of a long raw message
  • Improved the plugin-authoring skill's steps for sharing a mod: Claude asks public or private and checks the files before creating a GitHub repository
  • Improved the Skill tool's "Unknown skill" error to suggest a skill's listed name when Claude wrongly adds the anthropic-skills: prefix to it
  • Improved /reload-skills to say it re-sends the full skill list to Claude, which is how to get skills back after compaction
  • Improved the error shown when a worktree cannot be created because its base commit does not resolve: it now says how the lookup ended and the likely reasons, such as a repository without a commit
  • Improved the error for creating a worktree at a bare-repository layout's root: it now explains the layout instead of an unrelated git error
  • Improved artifact watching: a local session can now watch up to 25 published artifacts at once, up from 10
  • Improved background agent notifications: they now say when an agent is only waiting on its own background work, got a message too late for its result, or was stopped by a usage limit
  • Changed plugin hooks and workflow scripts to refuse values they hand back that nest deeper than 28,000 levels, with an error naming the limit (workflow scripts allowed 100,000)
  • Changed actions a plugin hook can block to be refused, not let through, when the hook cannot be handed them or cannot hand back its answer; a tool that already ran has its result withheld
  • Changed requests to claude.ai's connector proxy and to Anthropic-hosted MCP servers to no longer follow HTTP redirects; redirects by a connector's own server are unaffected
  • Changed MCP requests in cloud and self-hosted runner sessions to no longer follow HTTP redirects from the session's MCP proxy
  • Changed skill and command loading: one whose file or folder name has hidden, direction-changing or blank-like characters, < or > is no longer offered until renamed; such a name: is ignored
  • Changed ui.render trees in claude plugin test: each mod's Box or Text root now carries part: { plugin } naming the mod, so exact-tree assertions must include it
  • Changed WebFetch page reads to pick their effort as web searches do: the caller's level on the caller's own model, otherwise the level settings give the small model
  • Changed claude plugin test to fail a call to a mod's served $ method that has not answered within ten seconds, as a session does
  • Changed MCP allow rules to reach only the server they name: mcp__a no longer allows a server named a__b or a_; write mcp__<server>__* with the server's whole normalized name
  • Changed agent tools: lists to take only the named MCP server's tools; list a server whose name contains __ as mcp__<whole name>__*
  • Changed Claude in Chrome in Cowork cloud sessions outside auto mode: an approved-site action the safety classifier flags now asks you instead of being refused, unless managed settings apply
  • Changed cloud session and Remote Control MCP connectors to negotiate MCP protocol version 2026-07-28 by default on installs that fetch no flags; MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy opts out
  • Changed MCP tool descriptions and server instructions from Anthropic's first-party MCP servers at api.anthropic.com to reach Claude in full instead of being cut at 4,096 characters
  • Changed auto mode in Cowork cloud sessions: a PermissionRequest hook can no longer approve shell commands or subagents; those prompts wait or are denied
  • Changed the resume command printed at exit: it names the session by its ID and no longer by its name, so that nothing in a session name can run when the line is pasted
  • Changed the resume command printed at exit of a worktree session: it uses -w and -r if the long flags do not fit the terminal. If neither fits a kept worktree, rows above it say where to run it
  • Changed /btw side questions in non-interactive sessions to return a timeout error when still unanswered after 11 minutes
  • Changed UserPromptSubmit hooks to run before a skill or custom slash command expands, so a hook that blocks the prompt now also stops its embedded shell commands
  • Changed a skill's own front-matter UserPromptSubmit hook to first run on the prompt after the one that invokes the skill
  • Changed the turn.start mod hook to also hear subagents' and teammates' turns, not only the main loop's; tell them apart by e.agentId (absent on the main loop)
  • Changed the errors shown when /ultrareview can't upload a repository to stop suggesting git add ., which could stage or commit untracked files such as .env
  • Changed the cyber safeguard notice to no longer ask people to apply to the Cyber Verification Program
  • [VSCode] Fixed an unsent prompt and its attachments being lost when switching to another session and back
  • [VSCode] Fixed unused blank chats keeping a background Claude process running after starting a new conversation
  • [VSCode] Fixed the mic button showing an internal error message when you are signed out of claude.ai; it now offers to sign you in
  • [VSCode] Improved startup time in workspaces without a Python environment by starting Claude while the Python extension loads
  • [VSCode] Improved startup: the model picker and slash command menu now fill in right away in a new window on a folder you've opened before
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed a memory spike that could crash a session when many of its existing output files were re-sent to it at once
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed saving an edited routine silently moving it to a different environment when its own had been deleted or wasn't in the list; the routine now keeps its environment
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed Sessions search in a self-hosted environment's admin details finding nothing when you paste the session ID from a session's link
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed the Sessions and Runners lists in a self-hosted environment's admin details saying the list is empty when a search just has no matches
  • [Cloud sessions] Improved the deploy command shown when you create a self-hosted environment or environment key: it shows in full, wraps between arguments, and has a visible copy button
  • [Cloud sessions] Changed deleting a self-hosted environment to turn off its routines right away, with the reason shown on each routine, instead of leaving their runs to fail
  • [Remote Control] Fixed Remote Control sessions whose computer can't be reached still appearing to send your messages; your text now stays in the box and Send is off until it reconnects
  • [Claude Tag] Added the ability for Claude in Slack to delete a canvas it created in a channel when someone asks it to
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack staying silent on untagged posts that a channel's own instructions tell it to answer, such as posts that tag someone else, in channels with guests
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack reporting a reply to another channel's thread as posted when it isn't a member there; it now says the reply wasn't delivered and how to fix that
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack sometimes ending a turn without posting its answer when a self-hosted runner's image has no python3
  • [Claude Tag] Changed how Claude in Slack corrects a message it got wrong: it edits the message in place and adds a short "Edited" note instead of striking through the old text
  • [Claude Tag] Changed Claude in Slack to join channels with more than 100 members quietly, with no intro message
  • [Code Review] Fixed Code Review's monthly spend-limit comment and check-run card sending admins to Claude Code settings; they now link the Usage page, where that limit is set

  • Added $.prompt.media so a prompt.submit hook of a mod installed by managed settings can read the bytes of an image or document attached to the prompt
